description:
Found by defk-52v.3 (examples/lz4_snappy_decode.exs). The spec asked for ArgumentError "at the offending offset". raise takes a literal message only (raise-message), so the decoders raise a fixed message per kind of error ("lz4: match offset out of range") and the caller cannot learn where. Workaround today: return an error offset in a result tuple and raise in Elixir, which makes every kernel result a tuple and splits the error path.

Proposal: allow interpolation of i64 (and u64) expressions only, `raise ArgumentError, "... #{ip} ..."`: the C side formats with snprintf into the error term, Elixir mode is the interpolation itself. Strings, floats and other terms stay rejected.

Done when: the interpolated form compiles, both modes give the same message, docs/language.md raise section and the raise-message error entry are updated, and lz4_snappy_decode.exs reports the offset.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** A kernel's raise message may interpolate integer expressions: raise ArgumentError, "lz4: bad offset at byte #{ip}"

**Current behavior:**
`raise` in a kernel takes a string literal only; anything else is the compile error `raise-message` ("no interpolation or computed value"). Decoders (examples/lz4_snappy_decode.exs) raise a fixed message per error kind, so the caller cannot learn the offending offset; the workaround is returning an error offset in a tuple and raising in Elixir.

**Desired behavior:**
- `raise Exc, "text #{expr} text"` compiles when every interpolated expression is an integer (i64 or u64; narrower integer types too, as their values) in the kernel's subset. The native message is the decimal text of each value, exactly as Elixir's interpolation prints it (u64 above 2^63 prints as the unsigned value, negative i64 with a minus sign).
- Elixir mode produces the same message (plain interpolation), so assert_agrees compares equal.
- Interpolating anything else (a float, an array, a bitstring, a string, a tuple) stays a compile error under `raise-message` with a message that says only integers can be interpolated.
- Works wherever raise works today (including inside loops that yield, and after resume).

**Key interfaces:**
- `raise-message` entry in `Defk.Errors` (summary/why/hint) and the generated docs (docs/agents/generated-docs.md)
- docs/language.md raise section

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Tests: i64, negative i64, u64 above 2^63, several interpolations in one message, a message that is only an interpolation; native and Elixir mode give identical messages (assert_agrees)
- [ ] A raise with interpolation inside a yielding loop, under forced yields
- [ ] A float or array interpolation gives the raise-message compile error (compile_errors_test)
- [ ] examples/lz4_snappy_decode.exs reports the offending offset in its errors
- [ ] `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- Interpolating floats, strings or other terms; inspect-style formatting; custom exception fields

title: raise with an integer in the message: raise ArgumentError, "lz4: bad offset at byte #{ip}"
